risks: Minimal: review of existing records by clinical staff; no patient contact.
consent: Not sought: service evaluation of existing records under the research office classification and Caldicott approval.
data: Pseudonymised review forms; hospital numbers kept on the secure trust drive; results reported without identifiable cases.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: older patients, patients with limited English and patients whose index event was an emergency know least about their status and may be recognised least. Recognition is reported by age band, language where recorded and emergency status.
effectiveness: Useful if the committee learns whether the alert system improves recognition and where it fails.
efficiency: Existing records and trainee audit time.
costs: Trainee and consultant time within existing roles.
partnerships: Airway committee, emergency department airway lead, clinical informatics team and a patient partner who holds a difficult airway letter.
rebPath: Classified as a retrospective service evaluation (RSE-26-044) with Caldicott approval (CG-2026-118); no research ethics review is required for this scope.
limitations: Co-interventions, documentation of recognition and episodes outside the hospital.
summary: Records-only service evaluation with approvals in place and equity reporting.
